newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa says arms sale to China 'storm in teacup'.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa says arms sale to China 'storm in teacup'.

text.p: A South African firm said on Monday a report that it was negotiating a one billion rand ($220 million) arms sale to China was overblown, but revealed Beijing sent a delegation to the country last year.
"It's a storm in a teacup," Gordon Blackbeard, marketing director for Reutech Radar Systems, told Reuters.
"Reutech was approached by China for preliminary discussions and a delegation was received in May 1996 which indicated an interest in radar products...We've had nothing further since."
Blackbeard said his company was asked to provide a budgetary quote, after which "no technology transfer was sought or offered".
Reutech said the equipment assessed by China was a highly mobile two-dimensional radar system which it developed in cooperation with the government-controlled Armscor agency.

The weekly newspaper Rapport said on Sunday that China was negotiating with Reutech on a variety of high-tech arms and equipment, including two-dimensional radar, with the possibility of a later upgrade to three-dimensional scanning.

The state's National Conventional Arms Control Committee -- which vets all South African arms sales to foreign countries -- announced on Monday that it had not received an application on a possible deal with China from Reutech.
Cabinet Minister Kader Asmal, who heads the committee, told state radio its members had never even discussed a proposed arms deal with China.
Blackbeard confirmed Reutech had not approached the arms control committee, saying the discussions were so preliminary they had not necessitated a request for contracting approval.
